evidence: Cic. Inv. 1.48: crēdibile est quod sine ūllō teste audītōris opīniōne firmātur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Traupman also gives fidem habēre for “be credible”; the phrase more often means “to trust someone”.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 298.
